issues.description: Silent semantic change: `coerceNumber` replaces `identity` as the lift in `panLinear`/`zoomLinear`, altering behavior on non-numeric input.
issues.detail: The original used `toNumber` as lift and `identity` as ground. The new code substitutes `coerceNumber = toNumber(x) ?? 0`, converting `null`/`undefined`/unparseable values to 0 instead of propagating `NaN`. The PR claims 'same runtime behavior' but this is not true: a domain `[null, 10]` previously yielded `[NaN, ...]`; now it yields `[-5, 5]`. State this in the PR or preserve prior semantics.

issues.description: Loop/algorithm invariant is unstated: domain orientation (`d0 < d1`) and sign-consistency for `log`/`pow` are not documented or checked.
issues.detail: `panLog` and `zoomLog` compute `sign = Math.sign(domain[0])` and assume `domain[1]` shares the sign; if not, `log(sign)` produces NaN silently. The new `isNonEmpty` guard catches empty arrays but ignores the deeper precondition. A literate comment stating 'domain endpoints must be same-signed and nonzero for log/pow variants' would make this code readable and auditable.

issues.description: `Domain = [number, number]` return type is asserted but not proven; `lift`/`ground` may return NaN.
issues.detail: The return is typed `Domain` (two numbers), yet `log(sign)(x)` on a wrong-signed `x` yields NaN, and `pow(1/exponent)` on a negative result of a fractional exponent is also ill-defined. The type tells readers 'two numbers' but the algorithm cannot guarantee finiteness. Either tighten the type to `[number|NaN, number|NaN]` or add a postcondition check.

issues.description: `peek` overload ordering is correct but the file-level invariant deserves a one-line literate comment.
issues.detail: The overload `peek<T>(array: readonly [T, ...T[]]): T` correctly refines the return when the caller proves non-emptiness. Worth a single comment noting that callers who have already discharged the `isNonEmpty` check get the non-undefined return — otherwise a future reader will wonder why two signatures exist for a one-line function.

issues.description: Local `identity` shadows the removed import from `./accessors.js`; the rationale belongs in a comment.
issues.detail: The original imported `identity` from `accessors.js`. The new file defines a local `identity: TransformFn = x => x` because the shared one is untyped or has a different signature. A one-line comment ('local typed identity; shared accessors.identity is untyped pending TS migration') would prevent a future cleanup that re-imports and breaks types.

issues.description: Test coverage for the new precondition covers only two of eight public entry points.
issues.detail: `panLinear` and `zoomLinear` are tested for the empty-domain throw, but `panLog`, `panPow`, `panSymlog`, `zoomLog`, `zoomPow`, `zoomSymlog` share the same guard and are not exercised. A small table-driven test over all eight functions would discharge the invariant uniformly and protect against future divergence.

review.summary: The refactor is a straightforward, well-scoped TypeScript port and the `peek` overload is a tidy use of the type system. However, the claim of identical runtime behavior is not quite true: replacing `identity`/`toNumber` with a local `coerceNumber` that defaults to 0 changes how non-numeric domain entries propagate. The deeper preconditions — domain non-emptiness is now checked, but sign-consistency for log/pow and finite-output guarantees are not — remain unstated. Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED with a NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT tag. The types are an improvement; the invariants behind them deserve one more pass.
